_comment: Model-policy artifact for the DTS (Docker Compose) deployment target.
The DTS deployment calls a direct model provider (OpenRouter, an
OpenAI-compatible API) instead of AWS Bedrock. This file is the DTS
counterpart of bedrock-us-east-1.json: it pins the model matrix and the
per-token pricing used by the spend model. It is NOT scanned by the
Bedrock-access CI gate (that gate targets bedrock-us-east-1.json only) —
OpenRouter model IDs use the provider/model form (e.g. anthropic/...)
and the single-region-native-inference residency check does not apply.
There is no AWS regional pricing premium here: OpenRouter pricing is
flat/all-in per token.
Model matrix parity (issue #269): this file's primary/critic model_ids
must agree with model-policy/bedrock-us-east-1.json on role structure
and model family/generation per role (Opus-class primary, Sonnet-class
critic — see README.md's pinned matrix), allowing only provider-specific
ID syntax to differ (e.g. "anthropic.claude-opus-4-8" vs
"anthropic/claude-opus-4.8"). tests/lint-model-policy-consistency.py
is the CI gate that enforces this; keep both files in lockstep.
SOURCE NOTE (issue #269, verified 2026-07-13 against
https://openrouter.ai/anthropic/claude-opus-4.8 and
https://openrouter.ai/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6): model_id values and
cost_per_million_* rates below reflect OpenRouter's current listing for
Claude Opus 4.8 ($5.00 / $25.00 per million input/output tokens) and
Claude Sonnet 4.6 ($3.00 / $15.00 per million input/output tokens).
Re-verify against https://openrouter.ai/models before production use if
this file has aged past the pinned matrix's last update.
The model IDs may also be overridden per-deployment via the env vars
OPENROUTER_PRIMARY_MODEL_ID / OPENROUTER_CRITIC_MODEL_ID — an override
is honored by OpenRouterModelClient.invoke() but logged as an explicit
override (backend/src/model_client.py::enforce_openrouter_policy_model_id).
`selectable` (issue #445) is the ALLOWLIST an admin may pick from in the
app's "Model & API key" tab, stored in the model-settings table and
resolved by backend/src/model_settings.py. It exists so a deliberate
admin choice is possible WITHOUT weakening the runtime invariant that
enforce_openrouter_policy_model_id exists for: an arbitrary, unlisted
model is still refused before a request is spent on it. Resolution
precedence for an effective model id is admin selection > env override >
the models.primary/models.critic default pinned above.
`selectable` is deliberately NOT covered by
tests/lint-model-policy-consistency.py: that gate enforces Opus/Sonnet
family+generation parity with bedrock-us-east-1.json, which only the
DEFAULT pins are meant to satisfy. A non-Anthropic selectable entry
(Gemini, GPT, Kimi, DeepSeek) has no opus/sonnet/haiku family token by
design, and the Bedrock target has no admin-selection concept at all.
`tier` is CONSIDERED JUDGEMENT, not a benchmark result — the UI must
label it as guidance, never as a measurement. The cost rates ARE
computed facts and may be stated flatly.
SELECTABLE SOURCE NOTE (issue #445, verified 2026-08-02 against
https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models and .../models?zdr=true): every id
below was present in the live catalogue, listed a ZDR endpoint, and
advertised `response_format`/`structured_outputs` (non-negotiable — this
app requires strict JSON) plus `reasoning_effort`. Re-verify the rates
against that endpoint before landing a change here.
REASONING BUDGET (issue #527): `reasoning_max_tokens` on models.primary,
models.critic, and each `selectable` entry is the token allowance
backend/src/model_client.py::OpenRouterModelClient.invoke ADDS on top of
the pass's own content budget when it sends `max_tokens` — never carved
out of it. OpenRouter's `max_tokens` is a COMBINED ceiling across a
reasoning-class model's `reasoning` AND `content` tokens; a model given
no allowance can silently spend the whole budget on reasoning and return
empty content. An operator-run live probe (issue #527, 2026-08-03)
against real structured-output requests found exactly two of the eight
model_id values below reasoning-class — moonshotai/kimi-k3 and
google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview, both of which return `stop` with valid
JSON once given a several-thousand-token allowance; every other entry
returned 0 reasoning tokens at both a tight and a roomy budget. `0` is
the default for every model this file does not name an allowance for,
which keeps every currently-passing prompt fixture byte-identical.
CAPABILITY DESCRIPTOR (issue #562): optional per-model
`structured_outputs` / `prompt_caching` fields, read by
backend/src/model_client.py::openrouter_model_capabilities. Absent means
False -- fail-closed, never an assumed capability this file did not
actually declare. `structured_outputs: true` below on every `selectable`
entry is exactly the SELECTABLE SOURCE NOTE verification above (each id
advertised `response_format`/`structured_outputs`) turned into a field a
caller can read instead of only prose. `models.primary` / `models.critic`
declare neither field: that pricing verification (2026-07-13) predates
the capability check and never confirmed it, so this file has nothing
verified to assert for those two ids yet -- left absent rather than
guessed. `prompt_caching` is left absent everywhere in this file: no
verification pass has confirmed it for any OpenRouter-routed id.
PREFLIGHT ROLE (issue #491): `models.preflight` pins the cheap, fast
classifier the upload-time preflight check (backend/src/review_routes.py's
POST /api/reviews/preflight) uses to guess agreement type + paper side.
Deliberately its OWN role, not the primary/critic admin-selection ladder
(backend/src/model_settings.py) -- an admin picking a stronger primary/critic
model must never silently repoint this advisory, every-upload check onto
something expensive. Pinned to the Budget tier already in `selectable` below
(DeepSeek V4 Pro) rather than duplicated as a second selectable entry.
backend/src/model_client.py::openrouter_preflight_model_id resolves it
(OPENROUTER_PREFLIGHT_MODEL_ID env override, then this pin);
enforce_openrouter_policy_model_id accepts the pin the same way it accepts
the primary/critic pins. tests/lint-model-policy-consistency.py's
SHARED_ROLES tuple deliberately does not include "preflight" -- there is no
Bedrock counterpart to keep in lockstep (the AWS/Bedrock target has no
preflight concept yet); this role exists only on the OpenRouter/DTS artifact.
COVER NOTE ROLE (issue #499): `models.cover_note` pins the model
"Butter it" (POST /api/reviews/{review_id}/cover-note) uses to draft the
counterparty cover email from a FINISHED review's own analysis artifact
(issues[] + verdict_summary already on the reviews row -- never the raw
document, never a re-run of review). Deliberately its OWN role, same
reasoning as PREFLIGHT ROLE above: this is prose summarization of an
already-decided review, not legal judgment, so an admin's primary/critic
selection must never silently repoint it onto something stronger (and
pricier) than it needs. Pinned to anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 -- a
cheap-to-mid, non-reasoning (`reasoning_max_tokens: 0`) model distinct
from every other pinned role's model_id (primary=opus-4.8,
critic=sonnet-4.6, preflight=deepseek-v4-pro): issue #491 fix round 1's
lesson (a pin that happens to also be a `selectable` entry must still be
resolved and capability-checked through its OWN role, never only via
incidental selectable-set membership) applies here too, so
openrouter_model_capabilities' role loop and enforce_openrouter_policy_
model_id both name "cover_note" explicitly rather than relying on this
model_id also being selectable. backend/src/model_client.py::
openrouter_cover_note_model_id resolves it (OPENROUTER_COVER_NOTE_MODEL_ID
env override, then this pin), NOT run through the admin-selection ladder
(_resolved_admin_model_id) -- same non-admin-selectable posture as
preflight. tests/lint-model-policy-consistency.py's SHARED_ROLES tuple
deliberately does not include "cover_note" either, for the same reason:
no Bedrock counterpart exists for this role.

selectable.note: Frontier model from a different lab — a genuine second opinion.
About 15x cheaper than the highest tier.
